text: In 1830. <break time="0.8s" /> Only a few miles away. <break time="0.8s" /> From what is now the great city of Cincinnati. <break time="0.8s" /> Lay an immense and almost unbroken forest. <break time="0.8s" /> The restless pioneers. <break time="0.8s" /> Who had first settled the region. <break time="0.8s" /> Soon pushed farther west. <break time="0.8s" /> But a few of them remained. <break time="0.8s" /> And Murlock was one of these. <break time="0.8s" /> He lived alone. <break time="0.8s" /> In a small log house. <break time="0.8s" /> Surrounded on all sides by the forest. <break time="0.8s" /> Of whose gloom and silence. <break time="0.8s" /> He seemed to be a part. <break time="0.8s" /> He was never known to smile. <break time="0.8s" /> Or to waste a word. <break time="0.8s" /> And he supported himself. <break time="0.8s" /> By hunting. <break time="0.8s" /> And by selling animal skins. <break time="0.8s" /> In the river town. <break time="0.8s" /> His cabin had a single door. <break time="0.8s" /> And, directly opposite, a single window. <break time="0.8s" /> But the window was boarded up. <break time="0.8s" /> And nobody could remember a time. <break time="0.8s" /> When it was not. <break time="0.8s" /> Nobody knew. <break time="0.8s" /> Why it was closed. <break time="0.8s" /> And it was certainly not because he disliked the light. <break time="0.8s" /> For passing hunters often saw him. <break time="0.8s" /> Sunning himself on his doorstep. <break time="0.8s" /> I believe. <break time="0.8s" /> There are few persons living today. <break time="0.8s" /> Who know the secret of that window. <break time="0.8s" /> But I happen to be one of them. <break time="0.8s" /> As you shall see. <break time="0.8s" /> Murlock was said to be about fifty. <break time="0.8s" /> Yet with his white hair. <break time="0.8s" /> His long white beard. <break time="0.8s" /> And his deeply lined face. <break time="0.8s" /> He looked closer to seventy.
